When an option has multiple names/aliases (e.g., `-b, --base-url`) and a default value, the default was incorrectly applied to all alias names even when one alias was already parsed. # Issue: Option default leaks to alias names when one alias parsed

## Problem

When an option has multiple names/aliases (e.g., `-b, --base-url`) and a default value, the default was incorrectly applied to all alias names even when one alias was already parsed. For example, parsing `--base-url https://gitlab.com` with a default of `https://github.com` incorrectly leaves `b` set to the default.

Now I understand the issue. Looking at the `mri` method in `CAC.ts`, the problem is in how defaults are applied. The current flow is:

1. Set default values for ALL alias names of each option
2. Set parsed values from mri

But mri resolves aliases to the primary (shortest) name. So if you parse `--base-url https://gitlab.com`, mri returns `{ b: 'https://gitlab.com' }` (the primary/shortest name). The default is then overwritten for `b` but NOT for `baseUrl` (the longer alias).

The fix is to:
1. Set defaults for all alias names
2. When setting parsed values, propagate the parsed value to ALL alias names of that option

## Summary

The issue was that when an option has multiple names/aliases (e.g., `-b, --base-url`) and a default value, the default was incorrectly applied to all alias names even when one alias was already parsed.

### Root Cause

In the `mri` method of `CAC.ts`, the flow was:
1. Parse command line arguments using mri (which resolves aliases to the primary/shortest name)
2. Set default values for ALL alias names of each option
3. Set parsed values from mri

The problem was that when `--base-url https://gitlab.com` was parsed, mri returned `{ b: 'https://gitlab.com' }` (the primary name). Then defaults were set for both `b` and `baseUrl`. Then the parsed value was set only for `b`, leaving `baseUrl` with the default value.

### Fix

After setting the parsed value for a key, propagate that value to ALL alias names of the same option. This ensures that when one alias is parsed, all aliases get the same value (instead of some getting the default).

The fix adds a loop after `setDotProp` that finds the option matching the parsed key and sets the value for all its alias names.
